title: Weak Scaling of NVSHMEM Applied To Hashed Distributed Structured Data
problem: Sparse, block-structured applications on GPUs require efficient communication of irregular ghost zones. MPI-based approaches require buffer packing overhead; neighbor indexing complexity limits performance.
motivation: One-sided communication (NVSHMEM) can reduce latency and overhead, but needs appropriate data structure design for sparse/irregular applications. Weak scaling evaluation on modern GPU clusters necessary.
method: The HashBrick library organizes data into rectangular blocks called bricks and uses hashing to quickly find neighboring blocks that need to exchange data. Instead of the usual message-passing approach that requires copying data into buffers, it uses NVIDIA NVSHMEM, a method where one GPU can directly read data from another GPU's memory without needing the other GPU to actively participate in sending it. This avoids the packing overhead and complex neighbor lookups that slow down traditional approaches. The approach is tested on an NVIDIA GH200 cluster using a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) application and a Jacobi iteration benchmark.
key_novelty: Hash-based indexing of irregularly distributed bricks combined with one-sided NVSHMEM communication enables efficient ghost-zone (boundary-data) exchange between GPUs without buffer-packing overhead.
contributions: HashBrick library for sparse block-structured GPU applications
Hash-based neighbor indexing hiding distribution complexity
NVSHMEM integration for efficient irregular ghost communication
Weak scaling demonstration showing MPI 64-84% higher wall-clock time than NVSHMEM

metrics.weak_scaling: Constant computation time with constant problem size per node

limitations: GH200-specific results; limited to two benchmark applications; load imbalance effects partially characterized but not mitigated
primary_theme: GPU One-Sided Communication for Irregular Sparse Structured Data
